findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients type or scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. A realm that already enabled FGAP V2 for Users therefore keeps the old resource server, which has no 'Clients' all-resource and lacks the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Creating Clients permissions using those scopes then fails when their scopes cannot be found, and all-clients evaluation has no 'Clients' resource to evaluate, so the new Clients support does not work on already-initialized realms until the admin-permissions client is somehow recreated.

findings.title: Removal listener still dispatches to V2 when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The new guard only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but AdminPermissions.management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of V1. With both features enabled, a ClientRemovedEvent therefore calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, instead of the V1 cleanup the listener intends to run. The guard needs to exclude the V2 case, e.g. run only when V1 is enabled and V2 is not.

findings.title: Map-roles checks ignore manage permission and manage-clients admins
findings.body: canMapRoles(), canMapCompositeRoles(), and canMapClientScopeRoles() only check their exact FGAP scope for the client. Unlike canConfigure(), which first delegates to canManage(client), they do not treat a caller with the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role or an FGAP manage grant on that client (or on all clients) as able to map roles. Such a full client administrator can create, update, configure, and delete the client but is denied client role-mapping and composite-role operations under V2, breaking role administration for otherwise fully privileged admins.

findings.title: Global canView does not include an all-clients MANAGE grant
findings.body: canView() only checks the default role-based view check or an FGAP VIEW grant on the all-clients resource. A caller granted only MANAGE on all clients passes canManage() and canView(ClientModel) for each client (through canConfigure/canManage), and canView(ClientScopeModel) explicitly accepts MANAGE, but fails the no-argument canView(). Endpoints that gate on requireView()/canViewClientScopes()/canList-style global checks therefore return 403 for a manage-only administrator who is otherwise allowed to manage and view every client.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type, translating a user resource id to the username and the Users all-resource to 'All users'. Client resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for resources created by getOrCreateResource() is the client UUID, and the Clients all-resource is not labelled 'All clients'. Permission and resource representations for the new Clients type will therefore show opaque client UUIDs instead of the clientId, unlike the human-readable names provided for Users.
